title: About Endpoint Data Scan Sensitive Information: Exact Data Match

blocks.text: Exact Data Matching (EDM) utilizes a unique hybrid architecture to balance precision and performance. To learn more, see Understanding Exact Data Matching.
Unlike methods such as IDM or OCR that are processed entirely on the device, full EDM inspection requires the following approach:

blocks.item: A local prefiltering mechanism identifies candidate files on the endpoint.
Only the flagged candidate files are transmitted to the cloud for comprehensive evaluation.

blocks.text: EDM provides the following benefits and enables you to:

blocks.item: Identify and correlate multiple tokens that contribute to a particular record to identify data ownership.
Protect personally identifiable information (PII) from being lost.
Give your employees the ability to share their own PII data using a personal email or file sharing account.

blocks.heading: About the Exact Data Matching (EDM) Page

blocks.text: On the Exact Data Matching (EDM) Page (Data Security > Endpoint DLP > Endpoint Data Scan > Sensitive Information > Exact Data Matching), you can view the following:

blocks.item: Overview:
Total Number of Records: The combined count of all data entries across all active EDM prefilter files.
Total Size of EDM Pre-Filters: The cumulative size of all optimized prefilter files currently deployed to managed endpoints.
Users Allowed to Run EDM Optimizer: The specific administrators or users authorized to use the EDM Optimizer utility on their local systems to generate prefilter criteria.
Settings: Click to view the Settings page. You can add users who are designated to run the EDM Optimizer.
To add a user:
Click Setup User.
The Add User drawer appears.
Enter user details or select the user or admin in the Select User field.
See image.
Click Add.
The user gets added to the allowed users list. It is usually the admin who uploads the CSV file for cloud inspection.
Activate the change.
Ensure the Continuous Classification and EDM Settings are enabled in the Configurations tab. To learn more, see Configuring Endpoint Data Scan, Endpoint Settings, and Channels.
Filter data by File Name or Indexed By.
In the table, view information about the prefiltered file:
EDM Pre-Filter File Name: The unique name assigned to the generated prefilter criteria file.
Status: The current operational state of the prefilter (e.g., Active, Inactive, or Pending).
Number of Records: The total count of data rows processed from the source CSV file.
Number of Columns: The total number of specific data columns selected for prefiltering criteria.
Pre-Filter File Size: The size of the optimized file distributed to endpoints for local scanning.
Original File Size: The size of the source CSV file used to generate the prefilter.
Indexed By: The name of the authorized user who ran the EDM Optimizer to create the file.
Indexed Data: The timestamp indicating when the prefilter criteria were successfully generated and indexed.
Modify the table and its columns.
Select, deselect, or reorder the data fields displayed in the table.
Click the Edit icon to disable the exact data match prefilter file. You can also view information about the prefiltered columns (field names and data types).
See image.
Go to the Indexed Document Match (IDM) page.
Go to the Share Files Externally page.
